summary: Pietro Merlo (1850–1888) was an Italian linguist and Indologist. He studied at the University of Turin under Giovanni Flechia and Giovanni Maria Bertini, later teaching at the University of Naples and serving as professor at the University of Pavia from 1880.
Ping-kun Chen specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate at National Taiwan University (2001–2010), where he was appointed assistant professor in 2012.

Piotr Balcerowicz is a Polish Indologist and philosopher. He studied at the University of Warsaw, Banaras Hindu University, and the University of Hamburg, completing his habilitation at the Polish Academy of Sciences. He became a professor at the University of Warsaw in 2011.

Piotr Klafkowski (1953–2002) worked in Tibetology and linguistics. He earned his PhD at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań under Jerzy Bańczerowski and also studied under Lozang Jamspal, Geshe Geleg Gyatsho, and Nyalo Tulku Jampa Kelzang Rinpoche.

Piyanjali de Zoysa is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Delhi and the University of Colombo, where she earned her Ph.D. and was appointed Professor in Clinical Psychology in 1997.

Po Lu Khenpo Dorjé (1897–1970) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and his students included Taklung Tsetrul Rinpoche and Chagdud Tulku Rinpoche.

Poerbatjaraka (1884–1964) was an Indonesian scholar of linguistics, Indology, and archaeology. He earned his doctorate at Leiden University under Nicolaas Johannes Krom and later served as professor at Gadjah Mada University, the University of Indonesia, and Udayana University.

Polly Young-Eisendrath is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Ohio University, Goddard College, and Washington University in St. Louis, underwent Zen training under Philip Kapleau, and became a clinical associate professor of psychiatry at the University of Vermont in 1994.

Pongsit Pangsrivongse is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. After studying at Cambridge and earning a D.Phil. from Oxford, he worked as a Thai diplomat and became a PostDoc assistant at the University of Vienna in 2025.
Pooja Tomar is an Indology and philosophy scholar. She studied at the University of Delhi and Shri Mata Vaishno Devi University, where she earned her PhD in 2022 and worked as a research scholar.

Popatbhai Ambashankar Mankad was an Indologist and historian. His professional engineering appointments included State Engineer in Junagadh, Chief Engineer in Jodhpur State, and Chief Officer and Engineer for the Hyderabad Municipality.
Pori Park is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under Robert E. Buswell Jr. and held an appointment as assistant professor of religious studies at Arizona State University.

Potprecha Cholvijarn specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Bristol under Rupert Gethin and at Chulalongkorn University, where he served as a lecturer and became Chair of the MA in Thai Studies Program in 2024.

Poul Tuxen (1880–1955) was a Danish Indologist and philosopher. He studied at the University of Copenhagen, Leipzig, and Bonn under scholars including Dines Andersen, Hermann Jacobi, and Ernst Windisch, eventually serving as Professor of Indology at Copenhagen from 1928 to 1951.
Poulami Ray is an archaeology and history researcher who studied under Ranjit Sen. Ray is attested as a research scholar and fellow at The Asiatic Society in 2026.
Prabal Kumar Sen is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He held a professorship at the University of Calcutta (attested 2009) and was affiliated with the Ramakrishna Mission Institute of Culture.
Prabhasa Dharma (1931–1999) was a practitioner and scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under Zen teachers Joshu Sasaki and Seikaku Hirata.

Prabodh Chandra Bagchi (1898–1956) was an Indian scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He studied at Krishnagar Government College, University of Calcutta, and University of Paris under Sylvain Lévi, later serving on the faculties of Calcutta, Peking, and Visva-Bharati universities.
Prabodh Shirvalkar is an archaeologist and Indologist. He completed his Ph.D. in 2009 at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, where he was appointed assistant professor the same year.

Prachi Vatsal is an Indologist and linguist who completed her M.Phil. and PhD at Jawaharlal Nehru University (2016–2023). In 2025, she was appointed Sanskrit Educator at the Indian Institute of Technology Mandi.
